caveats: This check applies to in-use certificates and requires NotAfter more than seven days away. A non-ISSUED certificate without NotAfter is NOT_APPLICABLE; an ISSUED certificate without NotAfter is UNKNOWN.

iac.code: For an Amazon-issued certificate, keep the required DNS validation record and in-use service attachment under their real owners; review Private CA issuance permissions where applicable. For an imported certificate, the certificate owner obtains and reimports renewed material through the ACM console; an IaC declaration alone does not rotate it. iac.label: Update the actual certificate, validation, and service owners

references.title: AWS ACM check certificate renewal status

steps: Inspect the named in-use certificate in ACM Certificates > select certificate > Details and Renewal status, or use describe-certificate; record Type, Status, NotAfter, InUseBy, RenewalEligibility, RenewalSummary, and validation method before choosing an action.

For an Amazon-issued public certificate, repair failed DNS CNAME, email, or applicable HTTP validation with the domain owner and confirm ACM managed renewal; if renewal cannot complete before expiry, issue a replacement certificate and migrate each listener or distribution after validation.

For an ACM-issued private certificate, verify the issuing AWS Private CA remains active and can issue, the ACM service principal has renewal permission, and integrated associations remain eligible; coordinate certificate and client rollout with the CA and service owners.

For an IMPORTED certificate, obtain a renewed certificate and matching private key from its issuer through the certificate owner, then use ACM Certificates > select certificate > Actions > Reimport certificate to retain its ARN and associations; if reimport constraints prevent this, issue a replacement and migrate attachments.

Renew or re-import the certificate, or enable ACM managed renewal, before it expires. Verify NotAfter is more than seven days away, confirm TLS on every in-use association, and recollect the check; do not infer a safe renewal from absent metadata.
aws.c2b.acm.in_use_not_expiring_7_days.summary: For an in-use ACM certificate expiring within seven days, restore eligible managed renewal or reimport an issuer-renewed imported certificate before expiry.

caveats: Only certificates with nonempty InUseBy are evaluated. The failure set is exactly RSA-1024 or P-192 after underscore-to-hyphen normalization; other algorithms pass this predicate even if a consuming service has narrower support.

ACM reimport cannot change a certificate's key type or size. Imported and ACM-issued certificates need a new certificate ARN with a supported stronger key and an explicit migration of each InUseBy association.

Changing TLS certificates can break clients or renewals. Validate domain names, chain, service-specific algorithms, ownership and rollback before switching associations; the old in-use ARN keeps failing until detached.

steps: Describe the exact certificate ARN; inspect InUseBy, Type and KeyAlgorithm. An unused certificate is NOT_APPLICABLE; an in-use RSA-1024 or P-192 certificate fails after underscore-to-hyphen normalization.

Have the certificate and each consuming-service owner choose a stronger algorithm supported by that service. Request and validate a new ACM-issued certificate or import a new externally issued certificate under a new ARN; reimporting the old ARN cannot change key type or size.

Stage the new ARN in every InUseBy service association, verify TLS handshake, hostname and trust chain from representative clients, and retain the prior association for owner-approved rollback during the cutover.

Recollect the new and old certificate details. The old ARN remains a failed resource finding while in use; only after all consumers have moved does it become NOT_APPLICABLE, while the new ARN should pass the key-algorithm check.

iac.code: In the existing owner-managed ACM certificate, domain-validation and service-consumer declarations, review the exact issued certificate ARN and expiration against the captured 30-day boundary. Review a staged consumer cutover and rollback to the prior certificate before applying any change.
iac.label: Review certificate and consumer ownership

steps: Confirm the scan captured a complete regional ACM certificate inventory. Inspect the exact CertificateArn with DescribeCertificate and compare Certificate.Certificate.Status and NotAfter with context.created_at plus 30 days; an ISSUED certificate at the boundary fails.

If the issued certificate is within or at that window, identify its ACM-managed or imported renewal path, validation records, and dependent services with the certificate owner; do not infer renewal from RenewalEligibility or presume a live endpoint already serves a renewed certificate.

Have the owner validate renewal or stage a replacement/reimport and consumer cutover. Keep the previous certificate and attachment available for rollback until certificate status, expiration and client TLS behavior are verified.
Recollect the scoped inventory and rerun aws.nist.acm_all_certificates_expiry_30_days. Preserve NOT_APPLICABLE for a recognized non-ISSUED status and UNKNOWN for incomplete or denied evidence.
aws.nist.acm_all_certificates_expiry_30_.summary: Issued ACM certificate expires at or before 30 days after the scan capture instant. Inspect the exact ARN, renewal path and consuming services; have the owner renew or replace it with a validated rollback plan.
